title: fix(plugin-detail): the Reference Rail docblock names the live route, not the retired objectDef one
body:
Fixes #9816

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

`BuildPageOptions.showReferenceRail`'s docblock told authors to switch the Reference Rail on "per object via `detail.showReferenceRail`". Nothing performs that read. This package's own CHANGELOG records the objectDef `detail.*` block — naming `showReferenceRail`, `hideReferenceRail` and `hideRelatedTab` — as no longer consulted under ADR-0085, and `RecordDetailView` says the same at its synth call. An author following the sentence declared a key that does nothing: no warning, no degradation, no rail.

It is the third correction of the same claim. objectui#7998 corrected two README statements about this flag and PR objectui#9811 landed them; this one survived because it lives in source rather than in the document that sweep was scoped to.

## The repair

The parenthetical now names the live route only — the option on the synth call — and says what a per-page rail is instead: an authored `record:reference_rail` node in an assigned Page schema. The card left the shape open between "delete the parenthetical" and "redirect the reader"; the dispatch chose redirect, so a reader arriving from old metadata is told what replaced the route rather than merely un-taught.

The docblock's first sentence and its OFF-by-default / one-collection-query-per-related-list rationale are true and load-bearing, and are byte-for-byte untouched.

## The pin, and the trap it was written around

`packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/referenceRailRoute-9816.test.ts`. Nothing stopped that sentence rotting back, and it had already rotted three times.

It reads the two sides deliberately differently, because the subject here IS a comment:

- **The retired route** is asserted ABSENT over the RAW text of every file in this package, comments included — a comment is the carrier that bit all three times. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (it records what was once true); this test file is excluded by its own path, because it must carry the retired spelling as a fixture, and a discriminator re-derives that it is the ONLY carrier so the exclusion cannot quietly grow.
- **The live route** is asserted PRESENT over the source with whole-line comments STRIPPED. Over raw text that assertion would pass off the very docblock it is about — the shape measured inside objectui#7181's repair, green before the ablation and green after. The helper follows the `readCode` one in `scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.ts`.

**Both directions were ablated, each with the mutation proved on disk before the run and the restore proved by blob hash afterwards.**

| ablation | on-disk proof | result |
|---|---|---|
| put the defect back (restore the retired parenthetical) | retired-spelling count in the file 0 to 1; `ADR-0085` in the docblock 1 to 0 | **3 failed / 3 passed** — the package sweep, the sweep's discriminator, and the docblock pin all red |
| delete the live read (`options.showReferenceRail === true &&` to `true &&`) | live-read count 1 to 0 | **1 failed / 5 passed** — only the code-side pin red; the absence pins stayed green |

The second row is the trap, made visible. On that ablated file the raw text still mentioned `showReferenceRail` 3 times while the code side mentioned it once — and that remaining code-side mention is the member declaration, not the read. So a raw-text pin, and even a comment-stripped pin keyed on the bare key, would both have stayed green with the read deleted. Only the `options.showReferenceRail` spelling on the code side fails.

Restore after each ablation: `git diff HEAD` empty and the file's blob hash equal to `HEAD`'s.

## Measurements

Taken on a freshly fetched `origin/main` at `5365b4c344325baf05526ff7343be55465890842`, 2026-09-18T11:18Z, and re-taken at branch HEAD.

| probe | reading on `origin/main` |
|---|---|
| CONTROL — `options.showReferenceRail` in this same file | **hits** (one, in the rail gate) — the query fires and the live option is where the docblock's first sentence says |
| SUBJECT — any `detail.`-scoped rail key across `packages/`, excluding CHANGELOGs | the **only** hit is the docblock line this PR repairs |

After the repair, the same subject sweep over the whole tree returns only this PR's own two carriers: the pin's fixture line and the changeset's quotation of the sentence being removed. Both are outside the pin's population by construction.

## What the card listed as "not measured", now measured

- **Does any first-party schema, fixture or doc still author it?** No. The sweep above is tree-wide, not `packages/`-only, and finds no other carrier.
- **Do `hideReferenceRail` and `hideRelatedTab` carry the same parenthetical?** No — read at branch HEAD, neither docblock names an objectDef route, so neither was touched. The pin covers them anyway: its pattern is the `detail.`-scoped rail family, not one key.
- **Does the published `.d.ts` carry this docblock to consumers?** **Yes** — so the cost was larger than an in-repo reader, as the card anticipated. Measured on the real build artifact: after `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail build`, `dist/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.d.ts` carries the corrected docblock, and the retired spelling is absent from `dist/` with the docblock itself present as the control that makes that zero a reading. `dist` is this package's whole `files[]`, which is why this ships as a `patch` rather than an empty "no release" declaration.

## Verification

All commands run from the repo root in a dedicated worktree. Heavy runs serialized through the shared verify lock.

| run | verdict |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/` | **185 files / 1769 tests passed**, lock VERDICT command-exit 0 |
| every suite anywhere that NAMES the changed source file, outside this package (app-shell, components, apps/console, scripts) — enumerated by grep with a known-hit control | **9 files / 88 tests passed** |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` plus `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the new test file is in it) | exit 0, after building the upstream closure |
| `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-detail^...'` then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail build` | 11 tasks successful; package build exit 0 |
| `eslint` on the two changed files | 0 errors. The 60 warnings on the source file are all pre-existing `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`, none inside the edited docblock |
| `eslint .` across this package (the repo's own lint spelling) | 242 files, **0 errors**, exit 0; both changed files are inside that population |
| `check:test-path-roots`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:comment-mask-corpus`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major` | each exit 0 |

The narrowing is declared rather than assumed: repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` are CI's runs. Package-scoped lint is safe to narrow because this repo configures no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService` in `eslint.config.js`), so a file's verdict depends on its own bytes and the shared config — this diff cannot move an untouched file's verdict. The live Playwright spec that names the source file needs a running stack and is CI's as well.

## Acceptance notes

Noted, not filed — no card opened for any of these, and none is a defect:

- Running this package's lint with `--no-inline-config` (which is NOT how this repo lints — `pnpm lint` is `turbo run lint`, i.e. plain `eslint .`) surfaces two files carrying deliberate inline disables for `react-hooks/static-components`. Working as authored.
- `check:comment-mask-corpus` prints one disagreeing file within the residue objectui#7882 holds open. Pre-existing, report-only, already owned upstream.
- **No fourth instance of this rot exists.** The one other place in the tree that names the `detail.*` rail toggles — `RecordDetailView`'s comment at its synth call — states correctly that ADR-0085 REMOVED them. Reported rather than carded, per the dispatch.

## Out of scope, deliberately

`packages/plugin-detail/README.md` (objectui#7998 corrected it, PR objectui#9811 landed it, and it is inside another seat's in-flight objectui#8114 surface) — untouched. The retired objectDef reader itself is already gone under ADR-0085, so there is nothing to remove.
